title: Practices of Reliable Software Design
summary: Eight practices demonstrated by building an in-memory cache: favoring off-the-shelf solutions, reserving resources early, setting limits, and embedding performance counters.
when-to-read: Read when designing a new software component and weighing build-vs-buy, scope, or what observability/testing infrastructure to invest in upfront. Do not read for one specific named architecture pattern like functional-core/imperative-shell (see building-modern-architectures) — this is about general build trade-offs.
